children: Shares of Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
rose about 9% in premarket trading on Wednesday after the restaurant operator reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings that topped estimates and provided its fiscal 2027 outlook.
Adjusted earnings per diluted share came in at $0.99, above the $0.17 consensus estimate. Revenue was $849.3 million, also ahead of the $844.99 million consensus estimate.
fell 2.2% from a year earlier. Comparable-store restaurant sales declined 2.1%, while comparable-store retail sales increased 0.7%.

GAAP diluted earnings were $0.54 per share, while net income rose to $12.2 million from $6.8 million a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $62.1 million from $55.7 million, including a benefit of about $9.1 million related to tariff refunds, net of investments.

expects total revenue of about $3.36 billion at the midpoint, including comparable-store restaurant sales growth of around 4%. The company expects adjusted EBITDA of $190 million, commodity inflation of about 3%, hourly wage inflation of 2.75%, and capital expenditures of $117.5 million at the midpoints.
The company also said it ended fiscal 2026 with $337.2 million of total debt, down from $484.6 million a year earlier.
Shares have surged around 79% so far this year, far outpacing the 13.4% rise in the broader index.  Short interest on CBRL stands at 23.14% of the total float.

title: Cracker Barrel jumps after quarterly earnings beat, forecasts FY27 growth
